records.note: 'An information driven, AI enabled field in 5 years' names no entity, no observable event and no threshold. 'Information driven' and 'AI enabled' have no benchmark and no countable set, and 'therapy will matter ever more' is a comparative with no benchmark. The horizon 'in 5 years' would give 2027-03-09, but no event can be written to carry it.

'We're building out monitoring technology ... which i hope will allow us to scale up' is the forecaster's own team's build and its own deployment. Test (c) fails before the wording is examined: his own organization decides whether the monitoring product is built and used. 'Scale up the economic feasibility of deploying psychedelic medicine at scale' also has no threshold, and 'i hope' states a wish.

'We will similarly not like what's going to happen' with stimulants and later psychedelics names no body, no action and no observable criterion. A backlash with no named regulator, rule or enforcement action cannot be written as an event. Undated ('none').

'Psychedelic treatments are likely to make therapy more effective not just during but after' names no trial, no endpoint, no comparator and no effect-size threshold. 'More effective' is a comparative with no benchmark, so no trial_result event can be written.

'We're never gonna out lobby @Optum' gives no observable criterion: out-lobbying has no measure, no filing and no decision date. The rest of the tweet ('we need to create more compelling economic models') is normative. Optum is named, but nothing it or any third party decides is named.

A Texas policy on gender-affirming care and mandated reporting, and 'this will destroy healthcare in Texas'. Not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome for a drug, device or treatment in psychiatry, so test (e) fails. 'Destroy healthcare' also has no criterion.

records.phrase: It won't be paid for for another decade
records.stage_note: SAINT (Magnus Medical) received FDA clearance on 2022-09-06, the day before the statement, and had no published payer coverage policy at the statement date. base-rates.json has no class for a coverage decision, so b is null and the reference row abstains.
records.note: Payer call on SAINT the day after its FDA clearance. Mapped to E-0050: the same asset (accelerated TMS, whose asset text names the SAINT/SNT protocols) and the same outcome type (a US payer with national scope pays for it in the outpatient setting). Reading logged: 'it' = the SAINT neuromodulation system just cleared, and 'paid for' = a published coverage policy or announced payment arrangement of a national US payer; E-0016 is the same asset but a different outcome type (Medicare inpatient NTAP only). Deadline: 'for another decade' read through the anchor rule 'in a decade / in ten years' = statement date plus 10 years, 2032-09-07, origin anchor. Bin A on 'won't' with asserts false, per the denial rule ('will not X' is bin A with asserts false); p(E) = 0.1. Not affiliated: Magnus Medical and the payers are not in his affiliation list, and Fermata and Acacia are not named in the event.

'If we nail the payment model we will relieve suffering' has an antecedent with no observable criterion ('nail the payment model') and a consequent with no entity, metric or threshold ('relieve suffering'). Calling MDMA and psilocybin 'medical science success stories' is retrospective.

Value-based-care companies building their own EHR technology. EHR and value-based-care market structure is not a regulatory, trial, payer or practice outcome for a drug, device or treatment in psychiatry, so test (e) fails. No company is named either.

'You'll be hearing for more and more ERISA attorneys soon' is a quantifier ('more and more') with no countable set, and 'hearing from attorneys' is not an observable docketed action. The alleged Affordable Care Act non-compliance is not specified, so no complaint, defendant or claim can be written. 'Soon' is not a deadline in any case.

The target of 'this is never gonna work' is an unnamed startup in a parent tweet that was not fetched. With no entity and no observable criterion for 'work' or 'a PE play, but never venture', no event can be written.

'The DEA will require a license in EVERY state in which you will prescribe' restates the content of the DEA's February 2023 proposed telemedicine rule, which was published and open for comment at the statement date. The thread describes what the proposal says; it states information, not an expectation about a future DEA decision, so test (d) fails.

'Small molecules are probably not the future of care' gives no entity, no metric (prescription volume, guideline, approval count) and no threshold for 'the future of care'. Advice to trainees, not a writable event.

'@mindmedco will win' has no benchmark: no competitor set, no metric, no approval, trial or market threshold. A comparative without a benchmark is VAGUE, so the claim cannot be written as a company_event or trial_result.

His public comment to the DEA: a national telehealth prescribing program for controlled substances 'is not only necessary, but also timely', and 'would enable' providers to manage medications efficiently. 'Necessary' and 'would enable' argue for what the DEA should do; no future DEA action is asserted.

'Study will be stopped by IRB early' is about a hypothetical within-subjects withdrawal trial of a ketogenic diet for bipolar disorder that nobody has registered or announced. No sponsor, trial, registration number or IRB is named, so no event exists to write.
The acquisition target is an unnamed behavioral health startup in a parent tweet that was not fetched. Optum is named as the acquirer, but with no target company no company_event can be written.

'PE rollups will blow up in rapid succession' and 'venture funded healthcare will be an overwhelming failure' name no company, no countable set and no threshold. 'Blow up' and 'overwhelming failure' have no benchmark, and 'rapid succession' is not a deadline.

'79% remission ... will be our new standard at @FermataHealth and @AcaciaClinics' is a standard set inside his own organizations: Fermata (co-founder) and Acacia Clinics (clinician and trial site). His own organizations decide their own treatment standard, so test (c) fails.

'GLP-1 drugs will become part of the mainstay of the psychiatrist toolkit' gives no observable criterion: no guideline body, no prescription-volume series and no threshold for 'mainstay of the toolkit'. Unlike a guideline term such as 'first-line' (E-0013, E-0111), 'mainstay of the toolkit' cannot be resolved on a named source without inventing one.

'A hypothetical and neuro-modulated future where suffering is effectively alleviated' that 'changes expectations and payment models' names no payer, no code, no policy and no threshold. The forecaster marks it 'hypothetical' himself, and 'we're not prepared to do that yet' is a present-state judgement.

A trainee-doctor walkout in America, quote-tweeted from the South Korean resignations. A physician labour action is not a regulatory, trial, company, payer or practice-adoption outcome for a drug, device or treatment in psychiatry, so test (e) fails. 'This is coming' also names no countable set.

'Stringent REMS programs are in our future' does not name the drug or class. The parent tweet was not fetched, so the asset of the REMS cannot be written from the quote and its immediate context; guessing a class from a different tweet the same day would invent the asset. 'In our future' is not a deadline either.

'1T will be invested in these non solutions' carries a number but no referent: 'these non solutions' points to a parent tweet that was not fetched. With no asset, sector or named investment series, the quantity_threshold template cannot be filled.

records.phrase: It will not be just this that derails the approval for the combination therapy in question
records.stage_note: At 2024-06-10 the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) NDA for PTSD was under FDA review after the 4 June 2024 advisory committee voted against efficacy and against benefit-risk. Class: approval after a negative advisory committee vote (p 0.33, median 12 months). The item is undated, so the uniform 24-month window (to 2026-06-10) applies; 24 months is above the 12-month median, so b is not halved.
records.note: The sentence asserts that the approval is derailed and adds that more than one issue derails it. Mapped to E-0001, whose readings merge the first-cycle proposals on the Lykos NDA under review in June 2024 into the approval event on the asset; 'the combination therapy in question' and 'MDMA-AT' name midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy), the same asset. Asserts false: he denies FDA approval. Bin A on 'will', the strongest phrase in the claim sentence; p(E) = 0.1 after the denial conversion. No deadline words, so the item is undated. Not affiliated: Lykos Therapeutics and MAPS are not in his affiliation list.

The antidepressant is not named in the tweet and the parent tweet was not fetched, so the asset cannot be written. 'About SSRI minus (likely) sexual dysfunction, discontinuation effects' also gives no trial, endpoint or threshold, and 'will want to see what it looks like in the wild' defers judgement.

'In the future, it's going to come near home' names no device, no sponsor, no regulator and no count. 'Near home' has no criterion and is not the same as home use, so it cannot be written even as a device or market event. 'In the future' is not a deadline.

TMS as 'brain doping' for athletes in competitive sport. Cognitive enhancement in sport is not a psychiatric treatment decision, trial outcome, company outcome, payer decision or practice adoption, so test (e) fails. 'Hasn't caught on yet' also gives no countable set.

'Many places still do it once a day. I don't think that's the future' gives no metric for 'the future': no share of clinics, no guideline body, no coverage policy and no threshold that separates once-daily from accelerated TMS practice. No deadline words ('the future').

Two present-state statements: accelerated TMS gives 'a greater chance of remission' (a clinical generalization with no trial or endpoint) and 'insurance doesn't pay for it yet' (the coverage position at the statement date, followed by the CMS medically-unlikely-edit change he describes). No future coverage decision is asserted; 'yet' alone is not a forecast.

'If it were paid for tomorrow ... there would be businesses getting this to every patient everywhere the day after that.' The consequent has no entity, no countable set and no threshold ('every patient everywhere'), and the whole claim is put counterfactually. The antecedent (Medicare pays for accelerated TMS) is observable, but there is no writable consequent event to attach it to.

records.phrase: I'm dubious that we're going to have a durable version of TMS for ADHD
records.stage_note: At 2025-02-04 no FDA marketing authorization for a TMS device named ADHD in its indications for use; TMS for ADHD was at the investigational stage. base-rates.json has no class for a device authorization from the investigational stage (the 510(k) class covers clearance after submission, and no submission was named), so b is null and the reference row abstains.
records.note: Negative call on a named modality (TMS) and a named indication (ADHD), answering which conditions TMS will not help. Mapped to E-0063, the same asset (a TMS device for ADHD) and the same outcome type (the treatment becomes available through an FDA marketing authorization). Reading logged: 'have a durable version of TMS for ADHD' = an FDA-authorized TMS indication for ADHD from any sponsor, the observable marker of the field having a working ADHD protocol; the 'durable' qualifier is absorbed, since he gives no durability threshold. Bin D on 'dubious' ('doubtful' in the lexicon); 'I think' modifies 'I'm dubious', not the proposition, so it does not set the bin. Asserts true: the low bin already carries the doubt, p 0.3. No deadline words. Not affiliated: the FDA and the TMS device sponsors are not in his affiliation list.

'We have transcranial focused ultrasound coming online. Companies like Sanmai are bringing that technology to the fore' describes the state of the field at the statement date. No future decision, result or threshold is asserted; the finder records no confidence phrase.

A clinical generalization about retreatment after TMS ('90% plus of people are gonna respond to a second course'), stated about patients in general with no trial, no registry and no named data series, and expressly without 'the real numbers'. It describes how the treatment behaves, not a dated event, so the quantity_threshold template has no series to resolve on.

Press release on his own appointment as fractional Chief Medical Officer of Neurolief, about bringing Proliv Rx to patients with treatment-resistant depression. Neurolief (executive and advisor; Proliv Rx is a listed alias) decides its own launch and reach, so test (c) fails. 'Potential to reach millions' also has no threshold or date.

'Clinics like mine ... we're working hard on getting it published FDA cleared and most importantly covered by insurance subsequently' is a plan by his own clinics and the trial team he is an investigator on (Radial, Acacia Clinics). Publication and the submission are his own organizations' actions, so test (c) fails. 'Subsequently' is not a deadline.

records.phrase: really hard to imagine that this indication Brex[piprazole plus] s[ertralin]e for PTSD is going to get over the line
records.stage_note: At 2025-07-20 the Otsuka/Lundbeck supplemental application for brexpiprazole plus sertraline for PTSD was under FDA review, two days after the 18 July 2025 advisory committee voted 10 to 1 against. Class: approval after a negative advisory committee vote (p 0.33, median 12 months). The item is undated, so the uniform 24-month window (to 2027-07-20) applies; 24 months is above the 12-month median, so b is not halved.
records.note: Direct call on the FDA decision after the advisory committee vote. Mapped to E-0039: the same asset (the brexpiprazole plus sertraline supplemental application for PTSD) and the same outcome type (FDA approval). The auto-captions garble the drug names; 'Brex peppers all searchene' is read as brexpiprazole plus sertraline, per the video title and the advisory committee he is reviewing. Bin D on 'really hard to imagine', the lexicon D phrase 'hard to see'; asserts true, since the D bin already carries the low probability (p 0.3), and he says the decision, not the non-binding vote, is what is hard to imagine. No deadline words. Not affiliated: Otsuka and Lundbeck are not in his affiliation list.

'The closer TMS gets to being the first thing I'd recommend' states his own prescribing preference for younger patients. A statement of preference with no future state asserted; the finder records no confidence phrase.

'TMS works ... will make depression and particularly suicidality get better in most people we use it with' describes how the treatment performs in his own practice, not a dated event. 'Increasingly quickly' gives no metric, no series and no threshold.

Radial press release on Radial's own SWIFT publication; Radial is his employer (Chief Medical Officer), so test (c) fails. 'May help more patients start and complete' is also a quantifier with no countable set and no threshold.
